nodes.label: A 54-year-old man presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain and shortness of breath
Patient has a medical history of hypertension and subglottic squamous cell carcinoma, treated with cisplatin and radiation therapy 8 months prior
Physical examination showed signs of respiratory distress; the patient rapidly deteriorated, requiring intubation and hemodynamic support with norepinephrine, phenylephrine, and vasopressin
Hospital course lasted 2 months and was complicated by pulmonary embolism, atrial fibrillation, and gastrointestinal bleeding
Echocardiography, CT pulmonary angiography, cardiac biomarkers, and ECG have been requested but results are not yet available
The acute cardiopulmonary event may be due to pulmonary embolism with right heart strain and/or myocardial injury
Blood and fluid cultures returned negative
Abdominal CT and venous duplex have been requested but results are not yet reported
Acute cardiopulmonary event due to pulmonary embolism with right heart strain
Acute cardiopulmonary event due to acute myocardial injury/infarction
Acute cardiopulmonary event due to hemodynamically significant arrhythmia (new atrial fibrillation)
Acute cardiopulmonary event due to combined pulmonary embolism and myocardial injury
